question: A hemisphere is inscribed in a cube of side 6 cm. What is the volume of the hemisphere?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a hemisphere is inscribed in a cube, its diameter is equal to the cube's side length.

Radius of hemisphere (r) = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm

Volume = (2/3) × π × (3)³ = 18 × 3.1416 = 56.55 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 56.55 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Diameter of the hemisphere = Side of the cube = 6 cm

⇒ Radius (r) = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm

⇒ Volume of hemisphere = (2/3) × π × (3)³

⇒ Volume = (2/3) × 3.14159 × 27

⇒ Volume = 18 × 3.14159

⇒ Volume ≈ 56.55 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 56.55 cm³.**
